title: Chapter 2 Quiz 2
description: Algorithms that repeat, and algorithms that call themselves.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which type of algorithm uses a **loop** to repeat an action until a condition is met?
questions.explanation: Iterative algorithms use loops (while, for, repeat).

questions.question: You must add up all the elements of an array. Which type of algorithm fits this task?
questions.explanation: Repeating the same action for each element is the job of a loop.

questions.question: What does a **recursive** algorithm do?
options: It repeats a block with a loop
It solves a problem by calling itself on smaller sub-problems
questions.explanation: Recursion solves a problem by calling itself on smaller versions of the same problem.

questions.question: Which problems fit a **recursive** algorithm well?
questions.explanation: Recursion suits problems that break down into smaller, identical problems: trees, sequences, directories.

questions.question: Match each algorithm type to a typical use.
right: Summing the elements of an array
questions.explanation: Each family has its natural use case.

questions.question: An iterative algorithm repeats a block of instructions until a condition is met.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of an iterative algorithm.

questions.question: Iterative algorithms use loops such as while, for and {{1}}.
questions.explanation: The three kinds of loop: while, for, repeat.

questions.question: Complete the loop that adds the numbers 1 to 5.
questions.explanation: Each pass adds the loop counter i. EndDo closes the loop.
questions.hint: What changes on each pass of the loop?
